transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya T., Carlos I., Lina P. (Redwood) — Raj P., Emily N., Tomás R., Priya S. (Aurea)

Summary: quick procurement / legal handoff — Aurea's procurement and legal team walked through their acceptance criteria for MSA/DPA and SLA tiers, asked clarifying questions about private deployment and KMS, and validated the timeline for pricing approval. Redwood AE/SE provided an overview of which clauses are standard vs. negotiable, explained Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs, and agreed to follow up with a pricing worksheet and technical latency checks.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA data residency, SLA uptime and latency SLOs, KMS/HSM options, pilot commit and pricing pathway, onboarding playbook and timeline.

---- Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed, some errors expected) ----

00:00 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, AE, with Carlos our SE and Lina from CS.
00:06 Raj (Procurement): Hi, Raj here. We're running a vendor intake this quarter — happy to get through the playbook items.
00:11 Tomás (Legal): Tomás, legal counsel. We'll be focusing on MSA/DPA tight spots and any SLA exception paths.
00:16 Emily (Security): Emily, security. We'll want SOC2, key management and a list of controls.
00:20 Priya (ML): Priya, ML platform. I'll own the technical onboarding and pilot success criteria.

01:02 Maya: Great. Agenda — we'll walk through the redlines you sent, call out what's standard, what's negotiable, then Carlos will cover deployment options and expected latency/throughput. Finally we'll recap next steps. Okay?
01:12 Raj: Sounds good. Quick ask — can we get an initial pricing posture today? Even top-line. Procurement needs to know whether to go to pricing committee.
01:20 Maya: Sure, high-level yes — but final pricing needs confirmed committed capacity. I'll upload a worksheet after.

02:00 Tomás: On the MSA, the big items for us are data residency, indemnity caps, and audit rights. For DPA we want subprocessor visibility and minimum data deletion guarantees.
02:12 Carlos: On subprocessors — we publish a subproc list, and we can do a 30-day notice for changes. For deletion, for Hosted we can commit to logical deletion and purge windows; for Private deployments, you control the storage.
02:28 Emily: Clarify "logical deletion" — we need cryptographic erasure guarantees or ability to revoke keys. How does Redwood support KMS integrations?
02:36 Carlos: We integrate with major KMS providers — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and we have HSM partners for Private installs. For Hosted, Customer-managed key (bring-your-own-key) is available via KMS connectors, though there are a few latency and ops considerations.

04:05 Priya: If we do BYOK, will there be per-request key access that could add to latency for token generation? Our flows are latency-sensitive — sub-100ms for class A endpoints is important.
04:18 Carlos: Right, BYOK has an envelope encryption step. Typically that's a one-time session key unwrap for model weights or for storage, not per-token. But if you elect strict per-request key retrieval in the path, yes it can add tens of milliseconds. We can model that for you in a bench.

05:22 Raj: SLA — our vendor policy requires 99.95% uptime and P1 response within 15 minutes. Do you offer that for Hosted or only Dedicated/Private?
05:33 Lina: Hosted standard SLA is 99.9 with business hours support; Dedicated customers can get 99.95 and 24/7 support SLAs as part of reserved capacity. Private deployments we support via enterprise support add-on.
05:44 Tomás: For compliance we need an audit trail for every admin action — RBAC + immutable audit logs. Can you surface that in the Console or via API?
05:55 Carlos: Yes — Console has an audit stream, token-level traces and event logs. For Private, you can ship logs to your SIEM; for Hosted we maintain logs and can provide exports or cross-tenant audit copies depending on the DPA terms. Note: some log fields are abbreviated in auto-transcription — we'll send the log schema.

07:10 Emily: Data residency — Aurea needs EU-only processing for EU patient PII. Does Hosted support region pinning?
07:18 Maya: We do region pinning for Hosted — you can pin to EU regions. For guaranteed residency we usually recommend either Dedicated inside the region or Private deployment in your VPC.
07:28 Priya: If we pick Dedicated in eu-west, can we pin model variants and versions per environment? We want consistent quality across test and prod.
07:35 Carlos: Yes, Dedicated lets you pin model versions and rollout policies. You can control canary and A/B and rollback. We'll provide per-model performance profiles so you can baseline.

09:00 Tomás: There were a few redlines in the MSA we wanted to discuss: indemnity cap linked to fees is a no-go for us; we prefer a fixed cap. Also, there's a clause about data breach notification period — 72 hours is OK but we might ask for earlier notification for high-risk PII.
09:20 Maya: Understood — indemnity is negotiable within execs, we'll surface typical ranges. For breach notification we commit to 48 hours for PII and we'll flag legal for escalation. But I want to be transparent: some very aggressive terms (like contractual SLA credits beyond a point) need legal-level escalation.

10:40 Raj: Timeline question — procurement committee meets 6/30. If we get pricing and redlines before then, is that realistic?
10:47 Maya: Yes — we'll upload the redlined MSA template and the pricing worksheet by Friday 6/19. Carlos will have the tech run results by the 23rd, which should be fine for your committee.

12:05 Priya: On the pilot scope — we want to run a 4-week pilot, up to 2M tokens per month, with a success metric: 95th percentile latency below 200ms for our short-inference model. Is that doable?
12:19 Carlos: That feels achievable on Dedicated with the right GPU class and batching settings. For Hosted it might be tighter. We'll propose a configuration and expected cost/latency tradeoffs.

13:40 Emily: Any restrictions on storing prompts or embeddings that may contain PHI? We need to ensure we can opt-out of telemetry and prompts storage.
13:52 Maya: Yes — we offer telemetry opt-out for Enterprise tiers; data retention windows can be defined in the DPA for Private and Dedicated. Hosted has default retention but we can extend or turn off storage per contract. We'll include specific clauses.

15:30 Tomás: On subprocessors and subcontractors we want a 30-day right to object where changes expose new geo risks. You mentioned a list — can you share that?
15:40 Maya: We'll share the current subproc list and our update cadence. For any new subproc that affects data residency you'll get notice and can raise objections.

17:00 Raj: Pricing — high level: what does Dedicated vs Hosted look like in terms of committed monthly costs? We need a ballpark to evaluate supplier fee tiers.
17:10 Maya: High level, Hosted is variable usage; per-token. Dedicated has a committed monthly minimum with better per-token economics. For example, a mid-tier Dedicated pool for inference (x4 A100-equivalent nodes) might be in the mid-5-figure monthly range depending on model and concurrency. I'll put concrete options in the worksheet.
17:36 Priya: Any chargebacks for network egress or KMS transactions? We need to model egress fees.
17:44 Maya: Egress fees are typically pass-through depending on cloud region; we can provide cost modeling. KMS calls are not typically billed separately by Redwood, but if you use a premium HSM integration there may be a third-party cost.

19:20 Carlos: Quick tech note — when we say "KV cache" in docs, sometimes the transcript and folks hear "KV cash" — our implementation is per-request KV cache for autoregressive workloads to avoid re-computing token states; it also affects memory sizing.
19:36 Priya: Good to clarify — we'll add KV cache sizing to the pilot spec.

20:50 Tomás: A few DPA specifics: retention periods, right to be forgotten, and cross-border transfer mechanisms — do you support SCCs and Data Processing Addendum with EU Standard terms?
21:04 Maya: Yes, we support SCCs and an EU DPA addendum; for Private we can also add contractual clauses that mirror your enterprise policy. We'll send the DPA template.

22:30 Emily: Security evidence — can you provide SOC2 Type II attestation and penetration test summary?
22:38 Lina: Yes, we'll share SOC2 Type II report and a redacted pen test executive summary. For deeper diligence we can set up an NDA and a secure doc room.

24:10 Raj: Onboarding playbook — what's the usual sequence and how long? Our internal target is to have production in 8–10 weeks after contract.
24:20 Lina: Typical timeline: contract sign -> onboarding kickoff -> infra provisioning (2–3 weeks) -> pilot (4 weeks) -> production roll (1–2 weeks) — so 7–9 weeks is typical for Dedicated; Private on-prem can take longer depending on procurement and network. We'll tailor a timeline in the playbook.

26:00 Priya: Who usually owns network egress and peering setup? We prefer to keep VPC peering under our control.
26:08 Carlos: For Private deployments VPC peering is customer-owned. For Dedicated we can provision dedicated tenancy and we work with your network team on peering and egress rules.

27:45 Tomás: A clause in the MSA around indemnity for data subject claims — we asked for a carve-out if Redwood uses subprocessors. Is that something you'd accept?
27:55 Maya: We typically maintain responsibility for subprocessors we engage, but specifics can be reviewed. We will flag this to our legal ops for the redline.

29:40 Raj: Ok — procurement needs a clear acceptance checklist to take to committee. Can you produce a 1-pager with acceptance criteria: SLA target, security evidences, pricing band, pilot metrics, and contract redlines accepted as-is vs need negotiation?
29:55 Lina: Absolutely. We'll create an "Acceptance Checklist" one-pager and share it with you.

31:10 Priya: Slight aside — any limitations on function/tool-calling or streaming for our use cases? We're streaming multi-part responses for clinical summaries.
31:22 Carlos: Streaming is supported. Function calling has some constraints depending on the model. We'll surface model-specific guidance for streaming throughput and chunking.

33:05 Emily: About audit logs — we want an API to pull logs programmatically. Is that available?
33:12 Carlos: Yes, we expose the audit log export API; for Hosted we push logs to a customer endpoint or provide S3 exports.
33:30 Tomás: One more legal — termination for convenience clause, we want a 60-day notice not 90. Is that negotiable?
33:40 Maya: We can discuss; some enterprise terms allow 60 days with minimal penalties depending on the committed tier. We'll note this.

35:10 Raj: Anything that would block procurement from taking this to committee? From our side, if we have the redline, pricing worksheet, and acceptance checklist by Friday we're aligned.
35:22 Maya: That's our plan. Also we'll include a short risk memo: recommended Dedicated vs Hosted decisions given your residency and SLA requirements.

37:02 Carlos: I'll run the synthetic latency bench — I'll model both Dedicated and Hosted for your 2M token pilot, plus BYOK impacts. We'll include the 95th percentile numbers.

38:40 Priya: Great. If Dedicated meets the 95th<200ms metric at expected cost, procurement will likely push for Dedicated. If not, we may consider Dedicated + caching or edge routing patterns.

40:10 Tomás: On the DPA deletion guarantees, we want a contractual SLA for deletion within X hours. Is 24 hours feasible for logical purge?
40:21 Maya: We can commit to logical purge within 24–48 hours in the DPA; physical media sanitization timelines depend on infra and will be in the addendum. We'll propose 48 hours with an escalation path.

42:00 Raj: Any integration points for billing — we use a central billing code and need monthly invoices with line-item breakdown by token consumption / committed pool.
42:12 Lina: We provide detailed monthly invoices with token-level and model-level breakdowns for Dedicated and Hosted. For committed pools we can provide amortized unit costs.

44:00 Maya: Ok, recap of next steps — I'll upload: 1) Pricing worksheet and options; 2) redlined MSA/DPA template with callouts; 3) subprocessor list and SOC2/pen test docs; by Friday 6/19. Carlos will run the latency bench and share by 6/23. Aurea will provide a prioritized list of must-have security controls by 6/20.
44:28 Raj: Perfect. We'll slot this for the procurement meeting on 6/30.
44:36 Tomás: Thanks all. We'll review the docs and pick items that need legal negotiation.
44:40 Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the tech ride-along.

-- End transcript --
